I tested the iPhone 13 Pro way back in 2021 and noted how impressive Apple's video stabilization was. The feature has improved dramatically since then, and with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, Apple has introduced what it calls 'ultra-stabilized video'.

It may not be the flashiest feature, but it makes the iPhone much more usable for handheld video — something my latest testing has reinforced in a major way…

I own a small tripod and a GorillaPod, and always bring them along when I know I'll be shooting iPhone video. But one of the iPhone's biggest strengths is that the camera is always with you. Sometimes I spot something I want to capture but don't have a tripod to hand.

Often you can improvise, leaning the phone against a railing or steadying it against a lamppost. But there are times when you have to rely entirely on the iPhone's built-in stabilization, and I was genuinely surprised by how well it worked when I shot with the iPhone 18 Pro.

A boat trip along the Thames proved that the iPhone's built-in stabilization can actually look better than using a tripod. The boat was rocking so much that a tripod-mounted shot would have left the background swaying. The iPhone, by contrast, locked firmly onto the scenery outside, with only the boat itself moving in the foreground.

No matter how the platform moved, the horizon stayed perfectly level — something even a standard gimbal can't manage. Most consumer gimbals merely smooth out vibrations rather than eliminating them entirely. To truly lock the horizon, you need a high-end professional gimbal or the kind of gyro-stabilized mounts designed for boats and helicopters.

The iPhone 18 Pro's ultra-stabilization genuinely performs at that level, and it's available right in the native camera app without any accessories. That's seriously impressive.

Check out the demo clip below. If you don't want to watch the whole thing, the Tower Bridge section from here should give you the clearest sense of what it can do. But if you'd like a bit of London sightseeing atmosphere along the way, hit the C button for subtitles, which will show you the names of all the bridges and other notes, including a reference to Apple's UK headquarters.
